/-!
# Hilbert's Fifth Problem

The actual formalization is in `FormalConjectures.HilbertProblems.«5»`.

Hilbert's fifth problem asks whether every locally Euclidean topological group admits a Lie group
structure. This was resolved affirmatively by Gleason, Montgomery, and Zippin in 1952.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_fifth_problem)
- [Gleason 1952](https://doi.org/10.2307/1969548)
- [Montgomery–Zippin 1952](https://doi.org/10.2307/1969549)
- [Tao's blog](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/08/13/the-hilbert-smith-conjecture/)
-/

@[expose] public section

findings.description: The module docstring's references for the two 1952 papers link to the wrong DOIs. `[Gleason 1952](https://doi.org/10.2307/1969548)` resolves (Crossref; doi.org handle → jstor.org/stable/1969548) to K. Iwasawa, "On Some Types of Topological Groups", Ann. of Math. 50(3) (July 1949), p. 507ff. `[Montgomery–Zippin 1952](https://doi.org/10.2307/1969549)` resolves to E. Følner, "A Proof of the Main Theorem for Almost Periodic Functions in an Abelian Group", Ann. of Math. 50(3) (July 1949), p. 559ff. Neither is the cited 1952 paper; the Følner paper has nothing to do with the problem. The mathematics is unaffected: the file has no declarations, and the docstring's account of the problem and its 1952 resolution is correct.

review.notes:
The file under review contains no declarations. I enumerated the constants of module FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.HilbertFifthProblem in Lean and found 0. The file consists of a module docstring and an import. Its docstring says the actual formalization is in `FormalConjectures.HilbertProblems.«5»`. So no statement, `category` tag, answer or status in this file could be checked. The only findings possible are in the docstring, and the only defect is the pair of wrong DOIs reported above.

The docstring's mathematical claims agree with the sources:
- Wikipedia describes the modern formulation "in its simplest interpretation": is a topological group that is also a topological manifold isomorphic to a Lie group? It says this was solved by Gleason and Montgomery–Zippin.
- Tao's post states "Theorem 1 (Hilbert's fifth problem): Let G be a topological group which is locally Euclidean. Then G is isomorphic to a Lie group", attributed to Gleason and Montgomery–Zippin.
- Both papers appeared in Ann. of Math. 56 (1952).

I also checked that the pointer is accurate: `Hilbert5.hilbert_fifth_problem` in HilbertProblems/5.lean states the problem faithfully.
- The smoothness exponent `⊤ : WithTop ℕ∞` is `ω`, which is analytic (`contDiffWithinAt_omega_iff_analyticWithinAt`).
- The hypotheses can be satisfied: `Circle` with n = 1 elaborates.
- The extra `[T2Space G]` hypothesis is redundant. From `IsTopologicalGroup G` and `ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) G`, `ChartedSpace.t1Space` plus instance search gives `T2Space G`; I proved this in a scratch file. So the theorem says exactly that every locally Euclidean topological group is topologically isomorphic to a real-analytic Lie group.
- Taking the same n as the charts is harmless by invariance of domain, and passing from smooth to analytic is classical.
- The `research solved` tag matches the sources.

I did not review the Hilbert–Smith declarations in HilbertProblems/5.lean in depth, because they belong to a different file.
